page: Vultr vc2-4c-8gb is a Cloud Compute instance featuring 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyperthreading. Operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this server includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 160 GB NVMe SSD, and the network configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers. The shared Intel Xeon CPU delivers weak single-core and multi-core performance, scoring in the bottom 25% on stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read-only bandwidth reaches an average tier at 367.64 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write bandwidth falls into the bottom 25%. Computational tasks such as bzip3 decompression and text processing rank in the bottom 10%, and Redis SET operations achieve 2.63 million operations per second.

Given its shared CPU allocation and modest memory-to-core ratio, this server offers a budget-friendly entry point for workloads that do not require dedicated compute resources. It is suited for lightweight applications such as static web serving, basic development environments, and low-traffic testing environments. It is not recommended for memory-intensive databases, complex cryptography, or large-scale language model inference.
